title: Cursed!? - A fantasy-themed, solo blackjack.
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NX-1jJ1PuxY

Daniel (@dungeondive) bought Cursed!? from Goblin Hour Games through a Game Crafter crowd sale, largely on the strength of its red-and-sepia line art, and describes it plainly: fantasy solo blackjack, one player, three to six minutes, and a near-perfect travel game.

A witch will lift your curse for eight monster souls. Every card in the deck does three jobs — it is a monster with a power value that becomes your target number, a weapon with a damage value and a melee-or-ranged tag, and, on its reverse, an item. The same deck is also your hit points, so overshooting or stopping short costs you cards off the top, and running out ends the run. That single stack doing all the work is what he admires most about the design.

He plays a whole game on camera and loses with seven of the eight souls, which tells you more about the pacing than any rules summary. The items reward attention: a soul crystal that lets you bust without penalty, smoke bombs that shuffle spent cards back in, a whetstone, a backpack that fishes items out of the discard, and a mimic that turns into a monster the moment you draw it as loot. Daggers count as either one or six, declared on the draw — a real decision in a game this small.

----

Cursed!? makes one deck serve as monsters, weapons, loot and hit points at once. Which small games do the most with the fewest components?
